about.title: Personal Injury Help in Palm Springs, California
about.longDescription: Palm Springs sees its share of everyday traffic trouble. In the most recent full year on record, the city logged 268 injury collisions, with 390 people hurt and 8 lives lost on local streets. Corridors like Ramon Road, Rt 111, Indian Canyon Drive N, and Sr 111 (Gene Autry Trail) carry heavy public-record collision counts, and reports tend to cluster on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m., when tourist traffic, commuters, and weekend errands all converge at once. If you were hurt in one of these incidents, or in a fall, dog bite, or other accident somewhere else in the city, sorting out what comes next while you're still recovering physically can feel like too much. We handle personal injury claims for people across Palm Springs and Riverside County. Our team can review what happened and explain your options. There's no cost to talk it through, and we work on contingency, meaning no fee unless you recover. You focus on getting better; we'll sort through the paperwork.

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of an injury to file a claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity is involved. Talking to us early helps make sure you don't miss it.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you share some blame for what happened — your share of fault simply reduces, rather than eliminates, your recovery.

items.title: No Cap on Everyday Suffering
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in ordinary injury cases, so the impact an injury has on your daily life can be part of the conversation.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning our fee comes only from money recovered on your behalf — nothing out of pocket to start.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Palm Springs?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file most personal injury claims. If a government entity or vehicle is involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you were partly at fault. Your share of responsibility would reduce the amount you might recover, but it wouldn't bar you from pursuing a claim.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Palm Springs?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along corridors like Ramon Road, Rt 111, Indian Canyon Drive N, and Sr 111 (Gene Autry Trail), with reports tending to peak on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does your firm charge anything for a case review?
items.answer: No. We offer free case reviews to injured people in Palm Springs and Riverside County. There's no cost to you for the consultation itself.

items.question: Will I owe attorney fees if my case doesn't result in a recovery?
items.answer: We work on contingency, which means our fee is only collected if you receive a recovery. If there's no recovery, you typically owe nothing in attorney fees.
